Updated assessment incorporating the SLOOS: The FOMC statement remains clearly hawkish (75 bp hike to 3–3.25%, guidance of “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet reduction). The July 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows banks tightened standards and terms on C&I loans across firm sizes and on CRE, raised loan pricing and collateral requirements, and cited a weaker economic outlook—while household credit also saw tightening in several categories (credit cards, subprime auto, jumbo/GSE mortgages, HELOCs). Demand was mixed—stronger for C&I and HELOCs but weaker for several CRE categories. This tightening in bank credit supply is likely to amplify the restrictive stance of monetary policy, increasing downside risks to growth, capex, and CRE beyond what the FSR alone implied, even as bank capital/liquidity remain solid. Net: tilt the sentiment more negative than the FSR-only read.
